bodies.name: Eris
bodies.nativeSurface: Existing telescope detections and spectra do not resolve geography; replace the catalogue analog with a bespoke hypothetical map.
measured: JWST NIRSpec spectra show methane-rich surface ice and nitrogen-ice absorption; visible observations indicate a bright, approximately neutral-colour surface.
November 2010 stellar occultation constrains diameter to about 2326 km and high visible geometric albedo.
modelled: Interior thermal processing and surface refresh are proposed explanations for isotope chemistry, not resolved eruption observations.
unknown: No resolved global terrain map; geography, metre-scale relief, grain structure and precise visible colours are unknown.
True material reflectance and observer exposure/white balance are not calibrated.
Atmospheric variability, exact local terrain and sky appearance at a specified epoch.
assumed: Cold distant-epoch scenario with no optically appreciable atmosphere; pale methane/nitrogen frost covers a low-contrast hypothetical terrain.
Every crater, ridge and spatial albedo pattern is imagined; illustrative east-positive longitude is not registered to measured terrain.
Representative semimajor-axis illumination, not a dated landing. Hypothetical 60° camera field; subpixel Sun rendered with restrained glare, not an enlarged stellar disc.
Observer longitude and latitude are unspecified; moons and rings are omitted from the selected sky direction rather than given invented positions.

references.title: Grundy et al., JWST methane isotopes and nitrogen ice

bodies.name: Haumea
bodies.nativeSurface: Existing telescope detections and spectra do not resolve geography; replace the catalogue analog with a bespoke hypothetical map.
measured: Near-infrared spectroscopy identifies crystalline water ice; rotational photometry indicates a relatively dark reddish region.
2017 occultation constrains an elongated body and an equatorial ring; rotation period is about 3.9 hours.
modelled: Dark-region chemistry and geographic outline are not uniquely inferred from unresolved rotational photometry.
unknown: No resolved global terrain map; geography, metre-scale relief, grain structure and precise visible colours are unknown.

assumed: Water-ice-dominated ivory/neutral-grey surface, one subdued reddish-brown region with arbitrary map position and boundary.

bodies.name: Makemake
bodies.nativeSurface: Existing telescope detections and spectra do not resolve geography; replace the catalogue analog with a bespoke hypothetical map.
measured: Methane-rich surface with a red visible spectral slope; JWST spectra support additional hydrocarbon ices.
2023 January 29–30 NIRSpec observations analysed in 2025 detect methane fluorescence and volatile release.
2011 occultation rules out a dense global Pluto-like atmosphere at that epoch, not all gas.
modelled: 2025 gas interpretations include a tenuous bound atmosphere or expanding coma/plume; neither fully reproduces the data.
2024 mid-infrared excess may come from a small active region or dust ring; its origin and surface location remain unresolved.
unknown: No resolved global terrain map; geography, metre-scale relief, grain structure and precise visible colours are unknown.
True material reflectance and observer exposure/white balance are not calibrated.
Atmospheric variability, exact local terrain and sky appearance at a specified epoch.
assumed: Pale cream methane frost with muted ochre/peach-brown irradiation colouring and a few low-contrast darker patches. Colour saturation and spatial distribution are chosen.
A tenuous gas scenario with negligible visible sky scattering; no blue haze, thick clouds or visible plume. No unlocated hot spot, glowing lava or speculative ring is drawn.
Every crater, ridge and spatial albedo pattern is imagined; illustrative east-positive longitude is not registered to measured terrain.
Representative semimajor-axis illumination, not a dated landing. Hypothetical 60° camera field; subpixel Sun rendered with restrained glare, not an enlarged stellar disc.
Observer longitude and latitude are unspecified; moons and rings are omitted from the selected sky direction rather than given invented positions.

references.title: Protopapa et al., methane gas and hydrocarbon surface
Kiss et al., mid-infrared excess and alternative explanations
Grundy et al., methane-rich ice and isotope chemistry
